title: signalExplanation.ts: consume WaveScreen.showed_pullback_in_lookback/showed_rally_in_lookback to remove the ambiguous-Wave caveat
description:
Filed from api-stocks-analysis-wave-lookback's own checklist item 5 (that task's `decisions` entry explains why it wasn't folded into that backend task itself). GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis now exposes `screens.wave.showed_pullback_in_lookback`/`showed_rally_in_lookback` (bool | null, null only when `screens.tide.trend` is NEUTRAL) -- the exact `_wave_lookback` booleans `_determine_signal` (backend/app/signals/engine.py) actually gates BUY/SELL on, rather than just today's `screens.wave.state`.

`frontend/src/features/stocks/components/signalExplanation.ts`'s `explainSignal` currently has to render a `met: null` 'can't be confirmed from today's data alone' caveat for every HOLD case except the by-elimination one (see that module's own top-level docstring, 'The Wave lookback data-availability gap' section, for the full case breakdown). With the new field(s) exposed, every one of those cases can instead read the real value directly: `met: showed_pullback_in_lookback` (or `showed_rally_in_lookback`, depending on direction) whenever Tide is directional, with `met: null` genuinely only remaining for the Tide-Neutral case (where Wave was never evaluated against a direction at all -- already its own separate early-return branch in `explainSignal`, not the ambiguous-caveat one).

This is a real behavior change to a fairly dense piece of branching logic (the `waveMetToday`/`signal !== 'HOLD'`/`impulseMet && triggerMet`/else chain), not just a schema-typing update -- worth its own add-frontend-feature-skill pass (fixture/test rewrite across signalExplanation.test.ts, SignalExplanationContent.test.tsx's `ambiguousWaveScreens` fixture, and the module's own docstring) rather than folded into the backend task that unblocked it.

checklist.step: Rewrite explainSignal's wave-condition branch (frontend/src/features/stocks/components/signalExplanation.ts) to consume showed_pullback_in_lookback/showed_rally_in_lookback directly for every directional-Tide case, removing the 'other blockers' ambiguous-caveat branch entirely (met should never be null once Tide is directional -- only the Tide-Neutral early return should still produce met: null for Wave).
Update the module's own top-level docstring ('The Wave lookback data-availability gap' section) to describe the resolved behavior instead of the gap, or remove it if no longer relevant.

Update signalExplanation.test.ts's screens() fixture builder and test cases (and SignalExplanationContent.test.tsx's ambiguousWaveScreens fixture) to set showed_pullback_in_lookback/showed_rally_in_lookback explicitly per case and assert the new definitive met/detail text, removing coverage for the now-dead null-caveat branch.
Confirm SignalConditionExplanation.met's JSDoc ('null only for the Wave condition ... genuinely undeterminable') no longer applies, or narrow it to the Tide-Neutral case only.
Run frontend unit tests and the 90% coverage gate; update Storybook/browser-walkthrough coverage if task-qa-reviewer's checklist for this area expects it.

decisions.decision: explainSignal reads screens.wave.showed_pullback_in_lookback/showed_rally_in_lookback directly (picking the field matching the resolved direction) for every directional-Tide case, with a `?? false` fallback the code comments mark as defensive-only, not an expected path. The old three-way branch (waveMetToday / signal !== 'HOLD' / impulseMet && triggerMet / else-ambiguous) collapses to a two-way check: today's state matches (met: true, 'shows ... today'), else the lookback boolean is read directly (met: true 'showed one within the last 5 trading days', or met: false 'has not shown a qualifying ... in the last 5 trading days') -- no signal-dependent branching left, since BUY/SELL vs HOLD no longer changes which value is authoritative.
decisions.rationale: WaveScreen.showed_pullback_in_lookback/showed_rally_in_lookback are contractually non-null once screens.tide.trend is directional (see that field's own OpenAPI schema description and api-stocks-analysis-wave-lookback's decisions entry) -- the Tide-Neutral early return earlier in explainSignal already handles the only case where they're null, so by the time this code runs, direction is resolved and the field is guaranteed non-null. `?? false` is purely a type-level/defensive guard (the TS type is `boolean | null`) rather than a real fallback path the API is expected to exercise; throwing on an unexpected null was considered and rejected as disproportionate for a presentation-layer function -- silently treating an out-of-contract null as 'not shown' fails safe (renders a not-met claim) rather than crashing the balloon UI. A signalExplanation.test.ts case exercises this fallback explicitly for branch coverage, with a comment noting it's not a real API path.
decisions.alternatives_considered: throwing an Error on an unexpected null lookback value with a directional tide; keeping a signal-dependent branch structure mirroring the old code more closely

decisions.decision: The met:false Wave detail text no longer claims 'this is what's currently blocking a fresh BUY/SELL' (the old by-elimination wording) -- it now just states the fact ('Wave has not shown a qualifying X in the last 5 trading days'), letting the headline's 'missing: ...' list (which can now legitimately include Wave alongside Impulse and/or Trigger, since Wave's true state is read directly rather than only known by elimination) communicate whether other conditions are also unmet.
decisions.rationale: Once Wave's lookback value is read directly instead of inferred by elimination, it's newly possible for Wave to be false *at the same time* as Impulse and/or Trigger, a combination the old by-elimination branch structurally couldn't produce (it only set Wave to met:false when Impulse and Trigger were both already true). Keeping the old 'this is what's blocking it' phrasing would misleadingly imply Wave is the sole cause even when it isn't -- the neutral, factual wording is accurate in both the sole-cause and joint-cause case, and the headline already lists every genuinely unmet condition.
decisions.alternatives_considered: keeping the old 'this is what's currently blocking' wording only when Wave is the sole unmet condition, with a different string for the joint case -- rejected as unnecessary text-branching for marginal benefit over the headline already listing all blockers

decisions.decision: No Storybook story was added or changed for this task.
decisions.rationale: This task's changes are confined to a feature-scoped pure function (signalExplanation.ts, features/stocks/components/, not components/common/) and its existing test fixtures -- no new or changed common/ component was introduced, so the add-frontend-feature skill's Storybook requirement (Frontend.md §4) doesn't apply. SignalExplanationContent.tsx itself (which does render the explanation) was already a feature component with no story before this task and remains unchanged in this diff beyond its test fixture.
